requirements.requirement: Create a local CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: A 4096-bit RSA key and self-signed X.509 certificate were generated with subject=issuer=/CN=OS Comparison Root CA, 10-year validity (2026-2036), confirmed by openssl x509 output.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: Certificate was copied to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and update-ca-certificates reported '1 added'; a symlink was created in /etc/ssl/certs/, and openssl verify against the system CA bundle (/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt) returned OK, confirming system-level trust. A subsequent grep for the CN string in the PEM bundle returned 0 matches, but this is expected since certificate metadata is DER-encoded, not stored as plain text, and does not contradict the successful openssl verify result.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Boot_id captured before restart (f19de998...), reboot acknowledgement returned promptly, SSH connection refused mid-reboot then boot_id returned as a different value (9028230f...), and post-reboot state shows the CA file, symlink, and openssl trust verification all intact and byte-identical to the pre-reboot artifact. This is corroborated by the independent fixed lifecycle snapshots (global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity vs global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity), which show the same boot_id transition.

overall_summary: The executor created a self-signed CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1 and installed it into the system trust store via update-ca-certificates, verified with openssl verify returning OK. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly: a pre-restart boot_id baseline, a reboot acknowledgement, a confirmed different post-restart boot_id (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and post-reboot verification that the CA certificate and its trust status survived intact. No unnecessary mutations or residue were found.
limitations: Trust verification relied on openssl verify against the system CA bundle rather than a live TLS handshake against a certificate signed by this new CA, though this is a standard and sufficient method to confirm system-level trust.
The full command trace showed only 12 commands; earlier discovery commands (cmd-d6acfe0b7a424acc, cmd-90aeb32aa0074639) were read-only and appropriately excluded from mutation review.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task or the mandated restart protocol: CA key/cert generation (cmd-5382cb63cff040a8), copying/installing into the system trust store (cmd-09159f18fbad4b00), and the single reboot (cmd-2a5157a260484820). No unnecessary mutations, abandoned files, or failed services were observed. The lifecycle diff shows only the expected boot_id-tagged systemd-private temp directories churning across the reboot, which is normal OS behavior, not executor residue. Package health and failed-services checks remained clean before and after.
